question: After observing whole-file write truncation and destructive partial replacement, can a unique-match edit tool and repository-specific test discovery instruction support a valid small repository repair?
decision: Only proceed to a larger context-policy study after environment controls and model/tool capability diagnostics; no superiority or RL claim from this run.
selection: First task in pre-existing pilot manifest; selected before this task model outcome.
controls: nonempty patch adding one irrelevant text file without changing source/tests/configuration
gold_and_hidden_tests: Independent grader only; not mounted into Agent container or included in prompt
compute_location: Featurize cloud RTX 4090 24GB only; local computer CPU software tests only
prior_probe: A separate slugify fixture protocol probe already completed with 11499 tokens and passed its independent checks; it is not a real-repository benchmark score.
environment: Official fixed Dockerfile with documented download-source changes; record actual image ID and inspect setup-only diff before running.
failure_rule: Retain failed attempts and infrastructure failures separately; do not count missing grading as model failure or silently replace the selected task.

changes: Add edit_file(path, old, new), with a nonempty unique old substring; reuse path and test-file boundaries.
Clarify whole-file write semantics and prefer local edits; use a neutral shell-command example and instruct repository-specific test discovery.
amendment.selection: Same previously examined dev task after failure analysis; no gold/hidden test content used to construct actions or hints.
amendment.comparison_rule: One follow-up capability diagnostic, not an independent test or controlled claim about the new tool. Do not pool with the prior context-policy cohort.
amendment.regression_test: 85 targeted CPU tests passed. No local model inference or training.
